fruits.extendedStory: A stone carved in 985 credits work on Lisbon's walls to Almanzor. It calls the city a madina, which means a walled city, so the defences were already old news then. The castle has three ways in. The Main Gate crosses a stone bridge and the East Gate a metal one. The Gate of Betrayal was hidden, kept for a quiet escape in danger. After 1580 the castle worked as a barracks, a prison and a hospital, and the earthquake of 1755 left it badly damaged.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Eine Inschrift von 985 schreibt die Arbeiten an Lissabons Mauern Almanzor zu. Sie nennt die Stadt madina, also ummauerte Stadt. Die Burg hat drei Zugänge. Das Haupttor führt über eine Steinbrücke, das Osttor über eine aus Metall. Das Tor des Verrats lag versteckt, für den stillen Rückzug bei Gefahr. Nach 1580 diente die Burg als Kaserne, Gefängnis und Krankenhaus, und das Erdbeben von 1755 beschädigte sie schwer.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A stone carved in 985 credits work on Lisbon's walls to Almanzor. It calls the city a madina, which means a walled city, so the defences were already old news then. The castle has three ways in. The Main Gate crosses a stone bridge and the East Gate a metal one. The Gate of Betrayal was hidden, kept for a quiet escape in danger. After 1580 the castle worked as a barracks, a prison and a hospital, and the earthquake of 1755 left it badly damaged.

localizedStory.de: Eines der drei Tore heißt Tor des Verrats. Es lag versteckt, um unbemerkt hinauszuschlüpfen.
localizedStory.en: One of the three gates is called the Gate of Betrayal. It was hidden, kept for slipping out unseen.

fruits.name: Castelo de São Jorge
fruits.story: One of the three gates is called the Gate of Betrayal. It was hidden, kept for slipping out unseen.

fruits.extendedStory: The Sé goes back to 1150 and it is Romanesque, which means round arches and thick walls. That is why it looks so solid, more like a stronghold than a church. It is dedicated to Mary. Walk on to the Igreja da Conceição Velha nearby and the doorways change completely. Round and plain here, carved and curling there.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Sé geht auf 1150 zurück und ist romanisch, also Rundbögen und dicke Mauern. Deshalb wirkt sie so wuchtig, eher wie eine Festung als wie eine Kirche. Geweiht ist sie Maria. Geh weiter zur Igreja da Conceição Velha in der Nähe, dort sehen die Portale ganz anders aus. Hier rund und schlicht, dort verschnörkelt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The Sé goes back to 1150 and it is Romanesque, which means round arches and thick walls. That is why it looks so solid, more like a stronghold than a church. It is dedicated to Mary. Walk on to the Igreja da Conceição Velha nearby and the doorways change completely. Round and plain here, carved and curling there.

localizedStory.de: Die Kathedrale steht hier seit 1150, schwer und rundbogig, eher wie eine Burg gebaut als wie eine Kirche.
localizedStory.en: The cathedral has stood here since 1150, heavy and round-arched, built more like a fortress than a church.

fruits.name: Sé de Lisboa
fruits.story: The cathedral has stood here since 1150, heavy and round-arched, built more like a fortress than a church.

fruits.extendedStory: Until 1755 this was the Terreiro do Paço, the forecourt of the royal palace on the river. The palace stood here with the customs house, the mint, the arsenal and the Casa da Índia. An opera house had opened beside them months before the earthquake. A royal charter of June 1759 gave the rebuilt square its new name, the Square of Commerce. Eugénio dos Santos drew eight streets running north to south and nine crossing them. The bronze king on his horse is José, by Machado de Castro, finished in 1775.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bis 1755 war das der Terreiro do Paço, der Vorplatz des königlichen Palasts am Fluss. Hier standen der Palast, das Zollhaus, die Münze, das Arsenal und die Casa da Índia. Ein Opernhaus hatte daneben wenige Monate vor dem Erdbeben eröffnet. Ein königlicher Erlass vom Juni 1759 gab dem neu gebauten Platz seinen Namen, Platz des Handels. Eugénio dos Santos zeichnete acht Straßen von Norden nach Süden und neun quer dazu. Der Reiter aus Bronze ist König José, von Machado de Castro, fertig 1775.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Until 1755 this was the Terreiro do Paço, the forecourt of the royal palace on the river. The palace stood here with the customs house, the mint, the arsenal and the Casa da Índia. An opera house had opened beside them months before the earthquake. A royal charter of June 1759 gave the rebuilt square its new name, the Square of Commerce. Eugénio dos Santos drew eight streets running north to south and nine crossing them. The bronze king on his horse is José, by Machado de Castro, finished in 1775.

localizedStory.de: Das ganze Straßenraster hinter dir läuft auf diesen Platz zu. Acht Straßen führen vom Rossio herunter zum Fluss.
localizedStory.en: The whole grid behind you was drawn to end here. Eight streets run down from the Rossio to this square by the river.

fruits.name: Praça do Comércio
fruits.story: The whole grid behind you was drawn to end here. Eight streets run down from the Rossio to this square by the river.

fruits.extendedStory: Work on the wave pattern started on 17 August 1848 and ran until 31 December 1849. The waves vanished in 1919 and the square lost its sea. In 1979 the city council voted to bring them back, and the relaid Mar Largo came with the rehabilitation opened in 2001. The square's name changed twice, by decree in 1836 and by a city edict in 1971. The reason given was simple. The street signs had read Praça D. Pedro IV for years already.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Arbeit am Wellenmuster begann am 17. August 1848 und dauerte bis zum 31. Dezember 1849. 1919 verschwanden die Wellen, und der Platz verlor sein Meer. 1979 beschloss der Stadtrat, sie zurückzuholen, und das neu verlegte Mar Largo kam mit dem Umbau, der 2001 eröffnet wurde. Der Name des Platzes wechselte zweimal, 1836 per Dekret und 1971 per Erlass der Stadt. Die Begründung war schlicht. Auf den Schildern stand längst Praça D. Pedro IV.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work on the wave pattern started on 17 August 1848 and ran until 31 December 1849. The waves vanished in 1919 and the square lost its sea. In 1979 the city council voted to bring them back, and the relaid Mar Largo came with the rehabilitation opened in 2001. The square's name changed twice, by decree in 1836 and by a city edict in 1971. The reason given was simple. The street signs had read Praça D. Pedro IV for years already.

localizedStory.de: Schau nach unten. Die schwarz-weißen Wellen unter deinen Füßen heißen Mar Largo, von Hand verlegt und 1849 fertig.
localizedStory.en: Look down. The black and white waves under your feet are called the Mar Largo, laid by hand and finished in 1849.

fruits.name: Praça Dom Pedro IV
fruits.story: Look down. The black and white waves under your feet are called the Mar Largo, laid by hand and finished in 1849.

fruits.extendedStory: The lift opened in 1902 and it has been doing the same job ever since. It is 45 metres of iron standing in a narrow street, with the ornament of its time worked into every panel. That style is called Art Nouveau, all curling lines and plant shapes. Lisbon is built on hills, and this machine simply removes one of them for you. Walk up the street and you meet it head on, a tower where you expect a house.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Aufzug ging 1902 in Betrieb und macht seither dieselbe Arbeit. 45 Meter Eisen stehen in einer engen Gasse, verziert im Geschmack ihrer Zeit. Dieser Stil heißt Jugendstil, lauter geschwungene Linien und Pflanzenformen. Lissabon ist auf Hügeln gebaut, und diese Maschine nimmt dir einen davon ab. Geh die Gasse hinauf, dann steht er plötzlich vor dir, ein Turm, wo ein Haus sein müsste.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The lift opened in 1902 and it has been doing the same job ever since. It is 45 metres of iron standing in a narrow street, with the ornament of its time worked into every panel. That style is called Art Nouveau, all curling lines and plant shapes. Lisbon is built on hills, and this machine simply removes one of them for you. Walk up the street and you meet it head on, a tower where you expect a house.

localizedStory.de: Ein eiserner Aufzug, 45 Meter hoch, mitten in der Straße. Er bringt Leute den Hügel hinauf, den sie sonst steigen müssten.
localizedStory.en: An iron lift, 45 metres of it, standing in the street to carry people up the hill they would otherwise climb.

fruits.name: Elevador de Santa Justa
fruits.story: An iron lift, 45 metres of it, standing in the street to carry people up the hill they would otherwise climb.

fruits.extendedStory: This church was begun in 1241 and it carries the name of Saint Dominic. Inside, the style is Baroque, which means gold, curves and deep colour used without restraint. It stands a short walk from the Rossio, so you meet it almost by accident. The cathedral down the hill is round-arched and plain. Here the shapes swing.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Diese Kirche wurde 1241 begonnen und trägt den Namen des heiligen Dominikus. Innen ist der Stil barock, also Gold, Schwung und satte Farbe ohne Zurückhaltung. Sie steht ein paar Schritte vom Rossio entfernt, man stolpert fast hinein. Die Kathedrale den Hügel hinunter ist rundbogig und schlicht. Hier schwingen die Formen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This church was begun in 1241 and it carries the name of Saint Dominic. Inside, the style is Baroque, which means gold, curves and deep colour used without restraint. It stands a short walk from the Rossio, so you meet it almost by accident. The cathedral down the hill is round-arched and plain. Here the shapes swing.

localizedStory.de: 1241 begonnen und nach dem heiligen Dominikus benannt. Innen ist sie barock, also Gold, Schwung und reichlich davon.
localizedStory.en: Begun in 1241 and named for Saint Dominic. The inside is Baroque, which means gold, curves and a lot of it.

fruits.name: Igreja de São Domingos
fruits.story: Begun in 1241 and named for Saint Dominic. The inside is Baroque, which means gold, curves and a lot of it.

fruits.extendedStory: The stonework here dates from 1516. Manueline is Portugal's late Gothic, and it likes rope, knots and twisted columns where other styles keep straight lines. The church is low, about 15 metres to the top. Two other churches stand close by, one Baroque and one Romanesque. The three together make a lesson in stone.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Steinwerk hier stammt von 1516. Manuelinik heißt Portugals Spätgotik, sie mag Taue, Knoten und gedrehte Säulen, wo andere Stile gerade Linien halten. Die Kirche ist niedrig, etwa 15 Meter bis zum First. Zwei weitere Kirchen stehen in der Nähe, eine barock, eine romanisch. Zu dritt ergeben sie eine Lehrstunde in Stein.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The stonework here dates from 1516. Manueline is Portugal's late Gothic, and it likes rope, knots and twisted columns where other styles keep straight lines. The church is low, about 15 metres to the top. Two other churches stand close by, one Baroque and one Romanesque. The three together make a lesson in stone.

localizedStory.de: Stein von 1516, im manuelinischen Stil geschnitten. Das ist Portugals eigene Spätgotik, verschlungen, wo andere Kirchen schlicht bleiben.
localizedStory.en: Stone from 1516, carved in the Manueline style. That is Portugal's own late Gothic, twisting and knotted where other churches go plain.

fruits.name: Igreja da Conceição Velha
fruits.story: Stone from 1516, carved in the Manueline style. That is Portugal's own late Gothic, twisting and knotted where other churches go plain.

fruits.extendedStory: The house opened in 1793 and it was built for opera. José da Costa e Silva drew the plans. It stands on the Largo do Picadeiro. The square is small enough that you can be at the stage door without noticing the house. The Elevador de Santa Justa is a few streets away. One is iron and machinery, the other stone and song.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Haus wurde 1793 eröffnet und für die Oper gebaut. Die Pläne zeichnete José da Costa e Silva. Es steht am Largo do Picadeiro. Der Platz ist so klein, dass man am Bühneneingang steht, ohne das Haus zu bemerken. Der Elevador de Santa Justa liegt ein paar Straßen weiter. Der eine ist Eisen und Maschine, das andere Stein und Gesang.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The house opened in 1793 and it was built for opera. José da Costa e Silva drew the plans. It stands on the Largo do Picadeiro. The square is small enough that you can be at the stage door without noticing the house. The Elevador de Santa Justa is a few streets away. One is iron and machinery, the other stone and song.

localizedStory.de: Ein Opernhaus von 1793, entworfen von José da Costa e Silva. Seither wird hier gesungen.
localizedStory.en: An opera house from 1793, drawn by José da Costa e Silva. It has been open for singing ever since.

fruits.name: Teatro Nacional de São Carlos
fruits.story: An opera house from 1793, drawn by José da Costa e Silva. It has been open for singing ever since.

fruits.extendedStory: The tile panels here come mostly from the Fábrica da Viúva Lamego. One shows the Praça do Comércio as it looked before the earthquake of 1755. So you can stand here and compare a lost city with the one below you. The small church in the same garden was built in the 12th century, on the wall that once ringed Lisbon. From the rail you can find the Tagus, the port, the roofs of Alfama and the dome of Santa Engrácia.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Kachelbilder hier stammen großenteils aus der Fábrica da Viúva Lamego. Eines zeigt die Praça do Comércio so, wie sie vor dem Erdbeben von 1755 aussah. Du kannst also die verlorene Stadt mit der vergleichen, die unter dir liegt. Die kleine Kirche im selben Garten wurde im 12. Jahrhundert auf die Mauer gebaut, die Lissabon einst umschloss. Vom Geländer aus findest du den Tejo, den Hafen, die Dächer der Alfama und die Kuppel von Santa Engrácia.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tile panels here come mostly from the Fábrica da Viúva Lamego. One shows the Praça do Comércio as it looked before the earthquake of 1755. So you can stand here and compare a lost city with the one below you. The small church in the same garden was built in the 12th century, on the wall that once ringed Lisbon. From the rail you can find the Tagus, the port, the roofs of Alfama and the dome of Santa Engrácia.

localizedStory.de: Schau erst auf die Kachelwand, dann auf die Aussicht. Eine Tafel zeigt die Praça do Comércio, wie sie vor dem Erdbeben von 1755 aussah.
localizedStory.en: Look at the tiled wall before you look at the view. One panel shows Praça do Comércio as it stood before the earthquake of 1755.

fruits.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
fruits.story: Look at the tiled wall before you look at the view. One panel shows Praça do Comércio as it stood before the earthquake of 1755.

fruits.extendedStory: The fountain appears in writing in 1220, under King Afonso II, with a different name. It became the King's Fountain after the works of 1308, under Dinis. It stood against the city wall and carried six spouts shaped as animal heads. For a long time it was the capital's main supply of drinking water. In 1487 João II had it piped down to the sea, so boats lying at anchor could take on water.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Brunnen taucht 1220 in den Akten auf, unter König Afonso II., damals mit anderem Namen. Nach den Arbeiten von 1308 unter Dinis hieß er Brunnen des Königs. Er lehnte an der Stadtmauer und hatte sechs Röhren in Form von Tierköpfen. Lange war er die wichtigste Trinkwasserquelle der Hauptstadt. 1487 ließ João II. ihn bis zum Meer leiten, damit Boote vor Anker Wasser fassen konnten.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The fountain appears in writing in 1220, under King Afonso II, with a different name. It became the King's Fountain after the works of 1308, under Dinis. It stood against the city wall and carried six spouts shaped as animal heads. For a long time it was the capital's main supply of drinking water. In 1487 João II had it piped down to the sea, so boats lying at anchor could take on water.

localizedStory.de: Sechs Röhren liefen hier einmal, geschnitten als Tierköpfe. Zähl nach, was heute übrig ist: drei.
localizedStory.en: Six spouts once ran here, carved as animal heads. Count what is left today and you get three.

fruits.name: Chafariz d'El Rei
fruits.story: Six spouts once ran here, carved as animal heads. Count what is left today and you get three.

fruits.extendedStory: The house was built in 1868 to pump water, not to hold a museum. Its old name remembers a beach on this spot where ships came ashore to take on water. A fountain called the Chafariz de Fora stood here from the 16th century, the outside twin of the Chafariz de Dentro. The museum opened in 1998. Fado itself went onto the UNESCO list of the world's living heritage in 2011.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Das Haus wurde 1868 gebaut, um Wasser zu pumpen, nicht für ein Museum. Sein alter Name erinnert an einen Strand hier, wo Schiffe anlegten, um Wasser zu fassen. Ein Brunnen namens Chafariz de Fora stand seit dem 16. Jahrhundert an dieser Stelle, der Zwilling draußen zum Chafariz de Dentro. Das Museum eröffnete 1998. Der Fado kam 2011 auf die UNESCO-Liste des lebendigen Erbes.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The house was built in 1868 to pump water, not to hold a museum. Its old name remembers a beach on this spot where ships came ashore to take on water. A fountain called the Chafariz de Fora stood here from the 16th century, the outside twin of the Chafariz de Dentro. The museum opened in 1998. Fado itself went onto the UNESCO list of the world's living heritage in 2011.

localizedStory.de: Ein Wasserwerk, bevor es ein Museum wurde. Der Platz davor ist nach einem Brunnen benannt, und einmal reichte ein Strand bis hierher.
localizedStory.en: A pumping station before it was a museum. The square outside is named for a fountain, and a beach once reached it.

fruits.name: Museu do Fado
fruits.story: A pumping station before it was a museum. The square outside is named for a fountain, and a beach once reached it.

fruits.extendedStory: On 11 July 1726 fire took the warehouses that stood here. King João V had them rebuilt, and the west doorway by Fernando de Larre survives from that work. After the earthquake the Marquês de Pombal changed the plans again and handed the building to the army's arsenal. In the later part of the 19th century some of its rooms became a museum. Pedro Alexandrino and Bruno José do Vale had painted those ceilings.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Am 11. Juli 1726 vernichtete ein Feuer die Lagerhäuser, die hier standen. König João V. ließ sie neu bauen, und das Westportal von Fernando de Larre stammt aus dieser Zeit. Nach dem Erdbeben änderte der Marquês de Pombal die Pläne und gab das Haus dem Arsenal des Heeres. Im späteren 19. Jahrhundert wurden einige Räume zum Museum. Ihre Decken hatten Pedro Alexandrino und Bruno José do Vale bemalt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: On 11 July 1726 fire took the warehouses that stood here. King João V had them rebuilt, and the west doorway by Fernando de Larre survives from that work. After the earthquake the Marquês de Pombal changed the plans again and handed the building to the army's arsenal. In the later part of the 19th century some of its rooms became a museum. Pedro Alexandrino and Bruno José do Vale had painted those ceilings.

localizedStory.de: 1726 zerstörte ein Feuer die Lagerhäuser an dieser Stelle. Was danach entstand, ist heute ein Museum mit bemalten Decken.
localizedStory.en: Fire took the warehouses on this spot in 1726. What went up in their place is now a museum with painted ceilings.

fruits.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
fruits.story: Fire took the warehouses on this spot in 1726. What went up in their place is now a museum with painted ceilings.

fruits.extendedStory: Maria Severa Onofriana sang here, and the Mouraria has been called the cradle of fado ever since. She was born in 1820 and lived on the Rua do Capelão, the street you are standing on. A few steps on, the Largo da Severa marks her house with the words Casa da Severa. A Portuguese guitar is drawn into the calçada at your feet there. The plaque on the front was unveiled by Amália Rodrigues.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Maria Severa Onofriana sang hier, und die Mouraria heißt seither Wiege des Fado. Sie wurde 1820 geboren und lebte in der Rua do Capelão, der Straße, auf der du stehst. Ein paar Schritte weiter markiert der Largo da Severa ihr Haus mit den Worten Casa da Severa. Dort ist eine portugiesische Gitarre ins Pflaster gelegt, direkt vor deinen Füßen. Die Tafel an der Fassade enthüllte Amália Rodrigues.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Maria Severa Onofriana sang here, and the Mouraria has been called the cradle of fado ever since. She was born in 1820 and lived on the Rua do Capelão, the street you are standing on. A few steps on, the Largo da Severa marks her house with the words Casa da Severa. A Portuguese guitar is drawn into the calçada at your feet there. The plaque on the front was unveiled by Amália Rodrigues.

localizedStory.de: In diesen Gassen entstand der Fado. Geh weiter zum Largo da Severa, dort ist eine Gitarre ins Pflaster gelegt.
localizedStory.en: Fado was born in these lanes. Walk on to the Largo da Severa and you will find a guitar drawn into the pavement.

fruits.name: Mouraria - Berço do Fado
fruits.story: Fado was born in these lanes. Walk on to the Largo da Severa and you will find a guitar drawn into the pavement.
